_meta.indication: INCIVEK, in combination with peginterferon alfa and ribavirin, is indicated for treatment of genotype 1 chronic hepatitis C in adult patients with compensated liver disease, including cirrhosis, who are treatment-naive or previously treated with interferon-based treatment, including prior null responders, partial responders, and relapsers

pivotal_trials.population: Treatment-naive genotype 1 chronic hepatitis C subjects with compensated liver disease
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Sustained virologic response (SVR), assessed 24 weeks after last planned dose (SVR24)
pivotal_trials.n: T12/PR N=363; Pbo/PR48 N=361 (plus a T8/PR arm)
pivotal_trials.result: Overall SVR 79% (285/363) with T12/PR vs 46% (166/361) placebo/PR48; difference 32.8% (95% CI 25.2%, 40.4%)

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, open-label non-inferiority trial comparing 24 vs 48 weeks of peginterferon/ribavirin in eRVR subjects (non-inferiority margin 10.5%)
pivotal_trials.population: Treatment-naive genotype 1 chronic hepatitis C subjects
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Sustained virologic response (SVR) at 24 weeks post last planned dose (SVR24)
pivotal_trials.n: Overall enrolled N=540; of 322 randomized eRVR subjects, T12/PR24 n=162 and T12/PR48 n=160
pivotal_trials.result: In eRVR subjects SVR rates were similar: 92% (T12/PR24) vs 90% (T12/PR48); 24 weeks non-inferior to 48 weeks (95% CI -2.1%, 11.1%)

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled superiority trial (2:2:1) in prior treatment failures, with and without lead-in
pivotal_trials.population: Previously treated genotype 1 CHC subjects (prior relapsers, partial responders, and null responders); 662 enrolled
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Sustained virologic response (SVR) at 24 weeks post last planned dose (SVR24)
pivotal_trials.result: SVR with T12/PR48 vs placebo/PR48: prior relapsers 86% (246/286) vs 22% (15/68); prior partial responders 59% (57/97) vs 15% (4/27); prior null responders 32% (47/147) vs 5% (2/37)

key_safety: Most common adverse drug reactions (incidence at least 5% higher than controls) were rash, pruritus, anemia, nausea, hemorrhoids, diarrhea, anorectal discomfort, dysgeusia, fatigue, vomiting, and anal pruritus. Rash developed in 56% of subjects (severe rash 4%); serious skin reactions (DRESS, SJS) occurred in <1%; hemoglobin ≤10 g/dL occurred in 36% vs 17% with peginterferon/ribavirin alone
target_moa: Telaprevir is an inhibitor of the HCV NS3/4A serine protease, which is necessary for proteolytic cleavage of the HCV polyprotein into mature NS4A, NS4B, NS5A and NS5B proteins essential for viral replication; it inhibited recombinant NS3 protease with an IC50 of 10 nM

boxed_warning.content: No boxed warning; since there were no deaths related to telaprevir-associated rash, there will not be a boxed warning in the label

rems.type: DAVP and DRISK within OSE decided that a REMS was not required for telaprevir; a Medication Guide is part of labeling

advisory_committee.vote: The Antiviral Drugs Advisory Committee (April 28, 2011) voted unanimously 18-0 to approve telaprevir

summary.text: Telaprevir was granted fast-track status and submitted as a rolling NDA; it received a priority 6-month review because the Phase 3 trials showed superiority over standard of care, increasing SVR rates over 30% above current therapy. The Antiviral Drugs Advisory Committee voted 18-0 to approve, and the application was approved as a standard (non-accelerated) full approval.

citations.quote: Telaprevir was granted fast-track status and the NDA was submitted as a rolling submission. This NDA received a priority 6-month review because the results of the clinical trials showed that telaprevir when added to SOC was superior to SOC, increasing SVR rates to over 30% above that achieved with curr
Following discussion, the Committee voted unanimously, 18-0 to approve telaprevir.
